popular_belief: Hitters whose xwOBA (or xBA/xSLG) exceeds their actual wOBA (AVG/SLG) were unlucky and are buy-low breakout candidates; hitters far above their xwOBA are sell-high regression candidates.
how_commonly_held: Widely used framing: MLB's own glossary calls xwOBA 'more indicative' of skill than wOBA (S11), and x-stat gap lists are a routine feature of fantasy regression columns. Analysts who have tested it (S12-S16) disagree on how large the predictive edge is.
proposed_measurable_comparison: Rolling-origin out-of-time (OOT) forecasts for identical hitters. Baseline = Marcel-style weighted history of the target plus age plus PA forecast. Challenger A = baseline + multi-year xwOBA. Challenger B = baseline + (wOBA - xwOBA) gap. Outcomes: next-season wOBA (PA-weighted), AVG, HR/PA, R, RBI, Yahoo H2H points, 5x5 roto z-sum. Paired squared-error differences.
required_data: PA, AB, H, 2B, 3B, HR, BB, HBP, R, RBI, SB, AVG, wOBA, xwOBA, xBA, xSLG, sprint speed (control), age; seasons 2015-2025
published_evidence_before_our_test: S12: next-season R2 .221 for xwOBA vs .179 for wOBA; RMSE .0385 vs .0403; 65/35 blend .0378 (200+ PA pairs since 2015). S16: actual stats slightly ahead of expected stats for 2015-19. S15: the gap itself persists (year-to-year R2 .17). S14: first-half xwOBA vs second-half wOBA r = .406. S13: for pitchers, xwOBA no better than FIP.
notes: The main study already tests xwOBA for the wOBA target. We found no published test of whether the gain survives into fantasy categories or points. The straw-man version ('xwOBA alone beats projections') is not attributed to any source.

popular_belief: Barrel rate, exit velocity (average, fly-ball/line-drive, max or 90th percentile) and hard-hit rate flag power breakouts: rising EV or Barrel% predicts more home runs next season.
how_commonly_held: Common in RotoGraphs and draft-prep columns. Statcast power metrics are inputs to THE BAT X (S43) and OOPSY (barrel rate; S44).
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season HR/PA (PA-weighted) and HR count. Baseline = Marcel HR/PA x PA forecast. Challenger = baseline + Barrel%, max EV, hard-hit%, average EV (each alone, then jointly). Stratify by number of prior MLB seasons (1, 2, 3+).
required_data: HR, PA, Barrel%, exit velocity, max EV, hard-hit%, launch angle, sweet-spot%, ISO, age
published_evidence_before_our_test: S17: year-to-year r .82 (fly-ball/line-drive EV) and .80 (barrels per batted ball); this is stability, not incremental value. S18: an EV-gap screen alone gained +1.4 wRC+ vs +5.9 for controls; EV95 plus a contact gain gained +16 vs +7.
notes: Stability is not the same as incremental predictive value over prior HR rate. We found no published OOT test against a history-aware HR baseline.

popular_belief: FIP, xFIP and especially SIERA predict next-season ERA better than ERA itself, so ERA-minus-estimator gaps identify buy-low and sell-high pitchers.
how_commonly_held: Standard sabermetric teaching (FanGraphs Library) repeated in fantasy columns. The direction is not seriously disputed; the size of the edge is.
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season ERA (IP-weighted) for identical pitchers. Baseline = Marcel-style ERA with regression and age. Challengers = baseline + FIP, + xFIP, + SIERA, each separately. Also score IP-weighted fantasy ERA contribution (league ERA x IP / 9 - ER).
required_data: ERA, ER, IP, FIP, xFIP, SIERA, K%, BB%, GB%, HR%, age
published_evidence_before_our_test: S20: 2003-10 IP-weighted RMSE: SIERA 1.075, xFIP 1.089, FIP 1.141, ERA 1.308. S21: 2015-19 next-ERA R2: SIERA .204, xFIP .192, FIP .138, ERA .079. S22: 2007-18 starters: SIERA .193, prior ERA .11, projections about .22.
notes: FIP is a main-study target; ERA (a fantasy category) is not. This belief tests the fantasy-relevant version.

popular_belief: The signal in ERA estimators carries over to fantasy WHIP and to ratio-category value.
how_commonly_held: Implicit in fantasy columns that rank pitchers for ERA and WHIP with SIERA or xFIP. WHIP-specific published evidence is thin.
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season WHIP and IP-weighted WHIP contribution (league WHIP x IP - (BB + H)). Baseline = Marcel WHIP. Challengers = baseline + SIERA, + xFIP, + K-BB%.
required_data: WHIP, BB, H, IP, SIERA, xFIP, FIP, K-BB%, GB%, BABIP
published_evidence_before_our_test: S22: next-WHIP R2: K-BB% .294, SIERA .251, projections .238, prior WHIP .208, FIP .200. So WHIP is stickier than ERA and estimators add less.
notes: Pitcher BABIP regresses heavily (S37), so the hit component of WHIP is noisy. Expect smaller gains than for ERA.

popular_belief: K-BB% is the best single quick indicator of pitcher skill.
how_commonly_held: Frequently recommended in analytics-oriented fantasy writing (Pitcher List, CBS, FanGraphs Community). Its components stabilize quickly (S38).
proposed_measurable_comparison: Head-to-head single-metric additions to the same baseline on identical pitchers: K-BB% vs SIERA vs xFIP vs in-house Stuff+. Outcomes: next-season ERA, WHIP, K% and FIP, plus fantasy K count with an IP forecast.
required_data: K%, BB%, K-BB%, SIERA, xFIP, FIP, ERA, WHIP, K, IP, in-house Stuff+
published_evidence_before_our_test: S21: K-BB% R2 .224 vs SIERA .204 for next ERA. S22: K-BB% best for WHIP (.294) but behind SIERA for ERA (.176 vs .193). S20 did not test K-BB%.
notes: The main study tests K% and K-BB% for FIP and pitcher bWAR/200; the fantasy ERA/WHIP/K version is new.

popular_belief: Stuff+-type pitch-quality models stabilize within about 80 pitches and predict future pitching results, especially strikeouts and early-season changes.
how_commonly_held: Promoted in the FanGraphs Library (S23) and built into THE BAT X pitcher model (S43) and OOPSY (S44). Frequently cited in in-season fantasy columns.
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season K%, ERA, WHIP and FIP. Baseline (+K-BB%) vs baseline + in-house expanding-window Stuff+. If team IDs exist, split by team-changers vs stayers.
required_data: In-house Stuff+, velocity, spin, movement, extension, whiff rate, CSW, K%, BB%, ERA, WHIP, FIP, IP; team ID (not in the listed variables)
published_evidence_before_our_test: S23: Stuff+ reliable after about 80 pitches, Location+ about 400; Pitching+ beats preseason projections for relievers after about 250 pitches. S24: Stuff+ to next ERA .41 for stayers vs .14 for team-switchers; reliability .74.
notes: The study's Stuff+ is in-house, not FanGraphs Stuff+. Within-season stabilization cannot be tested with season-level data.

popular_belief: Fast runners (high sprint speed) are stolen-base targets, and since the 2023 rule changes speed converts into steals.
how_commonly_held: Speed as a steals signal is common in draft prep, and THE BAT X uses sprint speed (S43). Published analyses stress attempt rate, on-base opportunities and team intent instead (S27, S28). 'Speed alone predicts SB' is closer to a straw man.
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season SB (count and per opportunity). Baseline = Marcel SB + prior attempt rate (SB+CS)/(1B+BB+HBP) + OBP + PA forecast. Challenger = baseline + sprint speed. Test a sprint speed x post-2023 interaction. Also test the main study's baserunning-run-value forecast as a channel.
required_data: SB, CS, H, 2B, 3B, HR, BB, HBP, PA, OBP, sprint speed, age, season
published_evidence_before_our_test: S27: sprint speed vs SB% r = .298; vs attempts per opportunity r = .598 (2016-18). S28: attempts about 7% of opportunities with the base open (2024-25); team steal frequency 3.5%-11.6%. S26: SB per team-game rose from .51 (2022) to .72 (2023).
notes: The team or manager green light is not in the study data. The 2023 regime shift calls for a season interaction or a post-2023-only sensitivity check.

popular_belief: WAR is not fantasy value: defense, positional adjustment and replacement level do not score in fantasy.
how_commonly_held: Stated in fantasy columns (S30). We found no published source recommending WAR as a fantasy shortcut, so that opposite version is a straw man.
proposed_measurable_comparison: Does a forecast of hitter bWAR/600 PA (or its fielding and positional components) improve OOT forecasts of next-season roto z-sum and points beyond forecasts of wOBA and PA? Same question for pitcher bWAR/200 IP vs ERA/WHIP/K/W forecasts.
required_data: bWAR and its batting, baserunning and fielding run components; position; PA; IP; wOBA; R; HR; RBI; SB; AVG; W; SV; K; ERA; WHIP
published_evidence_before_our_test: S30: an April 2024 snapshot of 184 hitters found WAR overlaps AVG leaders and multi-category rank more than power or speed leaders. Informal; no OOT test.
notes: S30 itself reports partial alignment, so the counterview is 'WAR helps a little via AVG or playing time'. This belief directly informs how the paper frames its bWAR targets for fantasy readers.

popular_belief: Defense matters in fantasy only through playing time: good fielders keep their jobs and poor fielders lose plate appearances.
how_commonly_held: Appears in fantasy columns as a playing-time argument (S31). We found no quantitative published test.
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season PA. Baseline = Marcel PA + age + wOBA forecast + position. Challenger = baseline + prior fielding run value (rate and total). Then test whether fielding adds to counting-stat forecasts after conditioning on forecast PA.
required_data: PA, G, fielding runs (bWAR component), position, age, wOBA, R, HR, RBI, SB
published_evidence_before_our_test: None quantitative. S31 gives illustrative scenarios (cutting a player from 550 to 500 PA moves him from 96th to 129th).
notes: Lineup slot, depth charts and transactions are not in the study data.

popular_belief: Playing time is the dominant and most underrated driver of fantasy value and of disagreement between projections, and projections over-project injury-prone stars.
how_commonly_held: Widely repeated by projection authors and fantasy analysts (ESPN's Zola in S32; FanGraphs' Zimmerman in S33).
proposed_measurable_comparison: Decompose next-season fantasy value into PA (or IP) x per-PA (or per-IP) rates. Compare the OOT error reduction from an oracle PA vs an oracle rate. Then compare realistic PA forecasts (Marcel PA vs a constant) with metric-driven rate improvements.
required_data: PA, AB, IP, G, GS, all category stats, age; no injury data (use PA history as a proxy)
published_evidence_before_our_test: S33: PA RMSE 142-170 across systems; Marcel best; projections over-projected injury-prone hitters; adding injured-list information did not help.
notes: S47 is listed as nuance rather than rebuttal: accuracy studies score rates and AB/IP separately. Missing injury reports make this partly testable.

popular_belief: Ratio categories (AVG, ERA, WHIP) must be weighted by volume; a good rate over few AB or IP is worth little, and ratios matter as much as counting stats.
how_commonly_held: Standard in valuation write-ups (THT, RotoWire, Razzball). The opposite advice to 'ignore ratios' is described and rebutted in S35, but we found no published source that advocates it.
proposed_measurable_comparison: In simulated leagues built from realized seasons (Yahoo default roster and categories; NFBC 15-team), compare how much standings-points variation is explained by unweighted rate z-scores vs volume-weighted contributions (H - lgAVG x AB; lgERA x IP / 9 - ER; lgWHIP x IP - (BB + H)).
required_data: AB, H, PA, IP, ER, pitcher BB, pitcher H; league settings from S01 and S06
published_evidence_before_our_test: S35: AVG and WHIP are the most tightly bunched categories in NFBC standings. S34: worked example of scaling the AVG z-score by opportunity.
notes: Methodological. Needed so that metric gains in AVG, ERA and WHIP are scored as fantasy value correctly.

popular_belief: Points leagues and categories leagues value players differently. Points reward starting-pitcher volume, walks and extra-base hits; ESPN and CBS penalize batter strikeouts; relievers lose value; roto rewards SB scarcity and AVG.
how_commonly_held: Repeated in platform guides and fantasy primers every preseason. Yahoo now defaults new leagues to H2H points (S02).
proposed_measurable_comparison: Rank correlations of realized player values across Yahoo points, ESPN points (W = 2 and W = 5), CBS points (partial) and 5x5 roto. OOT incremental value of each candidate metric under each format.
required_data: All category stats; holds; CS; HBP (batters). Pitcher losses, quality starts and pitcher HBP are missing.
published_evidence_before_our_test: S08: 12 relievers vs 40 starters reached 350+ points in 2025 (format-specific counts). No OOT test of metric value by format found.
notes: ESPN points cannot include losses, and CBS cannot include QS, L or pitcher HBP; flag these as partial.

popular_belief: Extreme BABIP is mostly luck and will regress: pitchers toward league average, hitters toward their own career norms.
how_commonly_held: Core teaching in the FanGraphs Library and in fantasy regression columns.
proposed_measurable_comparison: OOT next-season AVG (hitters) and WHIP (pitchers). Baseline vs baseline + prior-season BABIP deviation from the player's career mean, with sprint speed and batted-ball-mix controls.
required_data: BABIP, AVG, WHIP, H, AB, HR, K, IP, sprint speed, GB/LD/FB mix, hard-hit%
published_evidence_before_our_test: S38: BABIP split-half stability point 820 balls in play (hitters) and 2,000 (pitchers). S37 is guidance, not a test.
notes: Overlaps H1 and H3; analyze as secondary. S37 itself notes hitters control part of their BABIP.

popular_belief: Average several projection systems; a consensus beats any single system.
how_commonly_held: Widely repeated by projection authors and in accuracy studies.
proposed_measurable_comparison: Not testable without archived third-party projections. Internal analogue: average of baseline and metric-augmented models vs each alone.
required_data: Archived preseason projections (not in study data)
published_evidence_before_our_test: S47: an equal-weight consensus ranked first in 2025. S45: a composite was best for 2025 wOBA. S48: in 2023 no system made a profit on the full player pool against market prices.
notes: Archived Steamer pre-season projections can be downloaded free (S51) if the authors want to extend this.
